subject: Renewal discussion: RapidCore pricing stability + commit shift
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@rapidcore.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal negotiation: pricing & credits

Hi Evelyn / Ben,

Thanks again for the hosted pilot support — usage spiked unexpectedly in Q2 as we ramped two large features. We need to lock in renewal terms by end of July to align with our budget cycle. Procurement has three asks: a 12-month price hold on current unit rates, a modest one-time credit to offset recent overage, and a commit path that lets us step up capacity without a long-term penalty.

High-level numbers: current run-rate ~ $48k/mo, Q2 peak was $110k. We’re targeting a 12–18 month plan but want flexibility in the first 6 months to true-up. Can you outline options for an interim credit and how a stepped commit would affect unit price? Also cc’ing Natalie from finance (looped separately).

Attachments: rapidcore-usage-Q2.csv (summary export)

Appreciate a clear list of next steps so I can bring to Procurement.

—Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Platform Engineering, RapidCore AI
alex.turner@rapidcore.ai
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@rapidcore.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal negotiation: pricing & credits

Hi Alex — thanks for the context and the usage file. I reviewed quickly and put together two structured options below to get you past procurement this month. I attached a one-page summary.

Attachment: renewal-summary-RapidCore.pdf (Renewal options matrix)

Option A — Stability + modest credit (recommended for immediate PO)
- 12-month price hold at current unit rates
- One-time credit equal to 20% of Q2 overage (applied to first invoice)
- True-up after month 6 with ability to convert overage to committed capacity at a blended rate
- No early termination charge for the first 90 days if you need to downscale

Option B — Commit-backed discount (better unit economics if you can commit)
- 12-month term with stepped commit: 3mo trial (no commit), 3–6mo partial commit (50% of projected run-rate), 6–12mo full commit (negotiated level)
- Unit price discounts scale with commit tiers (5% at partial, 12% at full)
- Upfront credit of $25k applied when contract activates

Next steps I suggest:
1) Pick option A or B for procurement (Option A is fastest).
2) If Option B, confirm target committed monthly run-rate so we can model pricing.
3) We’ll prepare an amendment + change order (DocuSign link) and a mutual action plan for onboarding capacity.

Ben — can you confirm availability to discuss a final commercial by Mon 20th?

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@rapidcore.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@rapidcore.ai>, procurement@rapidcore.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal negotiation: pricing & credits

Evelyn — thanks for the clear options and the PDF. Quick clarifications from Procurement and Finance: 

1) Procurement requires a committed PO amount by 31 Jul; they can route a PO for Option A value quickly but need us to confirm exact invoice timing for the one-time credit.
2) Finance will only accept credits applied as an invoice-level adjustment (not as future service credits) — can you confirm how you’d record the 20% overage credit?
3) Security ask: the legal team wants the amendment to reference our SOC2 evidence and the standard data processing addendum.

Also, we like Option B economically but need visibility on the pricing table for the stepped commit (numbers for partial and full tiers). Can Ben/Evelyn share a simple matrix that shows committed run-rate vs. unit price and the net-first-year spend for each tier?

Thanks — I’ll aim to get Procurement sign-off fast if we can provide the PO-ready language and numbers.

Alex / Team — great to hear you’re leaning in. I pulled together the stepped-commit matrix below and a suggested mutual action plan (MAP) to keep Procurement comfortable. I’ll send a formal line-item table in a follow-up but want these items on record now.

Stepped-commit pricing (illustrative)
- No commit (current): $0.012/token equivalent
- Partial commit (50% run-rate): $0.0114/token (5% discount)
- Full commit (target): $0.01056/token (12% discount)

Example: if you commit to $75k/mo at full tier, first-year net (after $25k upfront credit) = ~$850k (approx, we’ll provide exact calc).

Procurement MAP (high level)
1) Confirm option (A or B) and committed $ amount by 31 Jul (RapidCore)
2) Redwood to deliver amendment + PO-ready language (Evelyn/Legal) within 48 hrs of confirmation
3) RapidCore to send PO and PO number to billing@redwood.ai
4) DocuSign for amendment (Ben to send) and onboarding plan with CS (Marissa)

DocuSign draft: https://www.docusign.com/packet/AA12345
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/RDW-2319

Marissa — can you draft a 30/60/90 onboarding checklist for a capacity bump so we can tie to a canary rollout and monitor latency impacts?

Alex — we’ll mark Option B as preferred if you can confirm target commit; otherwise Option A gets a PO-ready one-pager today.

Best,
